Thady You Gander

Sounds very like “Leg of the Duck”, a very common jig in trad circles!

↳ Posted by Bannerman on November 5th, 2002.

Daniel of the Sun

This tune and “Thady You Gander” are similar and probably have the same origin, but I think they are different enough to be posted here separately.

I got this particular version from the recording of Finlay MacDonald. It comes from Duncan Johnstone, another Scottish piper. Some Irish settings like the one from O’Neill’s are available at JC’s, but in my opinion this one is simpler and the best.

I’ve never heard this jig played in Ireland, but is it common anywhere in the country?

↳ Posted by slainte on January 10th, 2003.

Played in Ireland

Yes, it is played in Ireland, but you wouldn’t hear it often. The late Micho Russell used to play a jig with the same title, though memory cannot recall whether this is the same tune. I suspect it is.

Domhnall Na Graine

https://thesession.org/tunes/7571

↳ Posted by hetty on August 6th, 2007.

I read an interesting story about the origins of this tune.

A man was very ill, and he wasn’t getting any better. One night, he stumbled out of his house in total frustration. He came upon a man in the street who asked why he was so unhappy. He told the stranger that he was ill and couldn’t recover. The stranger told him he had a tune. If the ill man would learn the tune from him, mastering it by morning his sickness would be gone. The stranger lilted the tune so that he could learn it. The sick man spent the rest of the night burning it into his memory. In the morning, he felt well enough to pick up his fiddle and play it. His sickness had gone.

Re: Daniel Of The Sun

I’ve played this tune for years, and have known it as Wee Murdie. It appears in the 1903-1908 David Glen Edinburgh Collection as “Thaddy You Gander”. In Glen, the last two bars in each part resolve to the low A rather than the B. I’ve always played it with the low A, which makes more sense to me. Nice old simple tune.

Re: Daniel Of The Sun

Lyrics from Doimnic Mac Giolla Bhríde’s album, ‘Guaillibh a’ Chéile’ with Griogair Labhruidh:

Comóradh ’s frolic thug Dónall a Bhálas
Do Dhónall na Gréine, cleasaí go tréarthach
Dá mbeadh sé seachtain i dtí leanna Rácáin
Cha dtiocfadh a‘n néal air, ’s b’annamh díchéille air.

D‘ólfadh sé dtuillfeadh sé, ’sa thuilleadh ’á ngeobhadh sé;
B‘fhearr i dtí ’n óil é, ’s ghabhadh sé ceol dóibh
Le feabhas a chuideachta mheallfadh sé an iomadaí,
Cailíní óga, díomhaoin is pósta.

Dónall na Gréine, giolla na péite,
‘gCuala tú a leithid d’alpurnach tréitheach
Leigheasfadh sé cailleach ar phlúchadh ’s ar chasachtaigh
’S gan teannadh uirthi ach sméideadh

Bhíodh Dónall ag ól leanna ’s a féin á cheannacht
Gan deoin na mbráthar, daoine gan náire;
Dhéanfadh sé pitséar a shuífeadh sa chistinigh
‘S a choinneochadh Genébha a d’ólfadh na ladies.

Bhíodh Dónall ar meisce ’sa bhean ag ól uisce,
’S na páistí ag béicigh, páistí ag béicigh.
D’ólfadh sé dtuillfeadh sé i gcuideachta a ngoidfeadh sé,
A chóta is a léine, a chóta is a léine.

Ba líofa a theanga i mBéarla agus Laidin,
Scriobhfadh sé Gaeilge, Dutch agus bréaga,
Le neart is a dhochar gur sháraigh sé an domhan,
Sin chugaibh cuid tréithe Dhónall na Gréine.
